title: Federico Fellini's birth chart
metaDescription: Federico Fellini's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 29.1° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Five of the ten placements whose signs are settled fall in cardinal signs, the widest weighting the unknown hour leaves certain. Cardinal weight opens doors — the chart of first movers and season starters.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 29.1° Capricorn — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by Mercury. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Capricorn and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 18.6° Capricorn, Venus holds 19.1° Sagittarius, Mars holds 25.4° Libra — in the old shorthand, a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun to Mars is the closest call of the day, a square within 3.7°. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, Venus trine Jupiter at 4.2°, and Mars trine Uranus at 4.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Saturn stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, two sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Moon in Capricorn at 20.4° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Libra at 25.4° is in detriment. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 4 in earth, 3 in fire, 2 in air, 1 in water by element, 5 cardinal, 3 fixed, 2 mutable by modality. Earth signs hold the scheme’s slow end, where results are measured in what survives rather than what starts. Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Capricorn for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.3° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 20.4°.
